newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland Fed U.S. median CPI up 0.2 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland Fed U.S. median CPI up 0.2 pct in Sept.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland said on Wednesday its U.S. median Consumer Price Index rose 0.2 percent in September.

The median CPI is a measure of inflation compiled by the Cleveland Fed that excludes items whose performance departs from the behavior of most components of the CPI released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The BLS's core CPI excludes only food and energy items.
In September the median CPI rose at a 2.1 percent annual rate. It was up 2.9 percent year over year, the Cleveland Fed said.
